body.en: Algebraic & Geometric Duality of \(\mathbb{C}\): Every complex number \(z = x + iy\) corresponds bijectively to a point \((x, y)\) in the Argand plane with modulus \(r = |z| = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\) and principal argument \(\theta = \arg(z) \in (-\pi, \pi]\). In exponential Euler form, \(z = re^{i\theta} = r(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)\), multiplication scales moduli and adds arguments: \(z_1 z_2 = r_1 r_2 e^{i(\theta_1 + \theta_2)}\).

body.en:
Why De Moivre's Theorem & Conjugate Root Pairing Hold: By Euler's identity \(e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta\), raising \(z = re^{i\theta}\) to the \(n\)-th power gives:

\[ z^n = \left(re^{i\theta}\right)^n = r^n e^{in\theta} = r^n(\cos(n\theta) + i\sin(n\theta)) \]

Furthermore, if \(P(z) = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k z^k\) has real coefficients (\(a_k \in \mathbb{R}\)), taking complex conjugates across \(P(z_0) = 0\) uses \(\overline{z_1 + z_2} = \bar{z}_1 + \bar{z}_2\) and \(\bar{a}_k = a_k\) to prove \(P(\bar{z}_0) = \overline{P(z_0)} = 0\). Thus non-real roots of real polynomials always occur in conjugate pairs \(\alpha \pm i\beta\).
body.ar:

\[ z^n = \left(re^{i\theta}\right)^n = r^n e^{in\theta} = r^n(\cos(n\theta) + i\sin(n\theta)) \]

Furthermore, if \(P(z) = \sum_{k=0}^n a_k z^k\) has real المعاملات (\(a_k \in \mathbb{R}\)), taking complex conjugates across \(P(z_0) = 0\) uses \(\overline{z_1 + z_2} = \bar{z}_1 + \bar{z}_2\) and \(\bar{a}_k = a_k\) to prove \(P(\bar{z}_0) = \overline{P(z_0)} = 0\). وعليه non-real roots of real polynomials always occur in conjugate pairs \(\alpha \pm i\beta\).

body.en:
Describe the roots of \( x^{2}+2x+5=0 \).

Discriminant \Delta=2^{2}-4(1)(5)=-16<0 , so there are no real roots — two complex conjugates. Solving:

\[ x=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{-16}}{2}=-1\pm 2i. \]

body.en:
• Powers of i Cycle: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\). For high powers \(i^n\), divide the exponent \(n\) by 4 and evaluate using the remainder (e.g. \(i^{27} = i^{4(6)+3} = i^3 = -i\)).
  • Multiplying Negative Radicals: Never write \(\sqrt{-3}\sqrt{-12} = \sqrt{36} = 6\)! You must extract the imaginary unit first: \((i\sqrt{3})(i\sqrt{12}) = i^2\sqrt{36} = -1(6) = -6\).
  • Discriminant Interpretation: For \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\): if \(\Delta > 0\), two distinct real roots; if \(\Delta = 0\), one repeated real rational root (vertex on \(x\)-axis); if \(\Delta < 0\), two non-real complex conjugate roots \(a \pm bi\).
  • Completing the Square with \(a \neq 1\): Always factor the leading coefficient \(a\) out of the quadratic and linear terms before adding \((b/(2a))^2\). In \(2x^2 - 12x\), factor to \(2(x^2 - 6x)\), then add 9 inside the parentheses (which actually adds \(2 \times 9 = 18\) to that side).
body.ar:
• Powers of i Cycle: \(i^1 = i\), \(i^2 = -1\), \(i^3 = -i\), \(i^4 = 1\). For high powers \(i^n\), divide the exponent \(n\) by 4 and احسب قيمة using the remainder (e.g. \(i^{27} = i^{4(6)+3} = i^3 = -i\)).
  • Multiplying Negative Radicals: Never write \(\sqrt{-3}\sqrt{-12} = \sqrt{36} = 6\)! You must extract the imaginary unit first: \((i\sqrt{3})(i\sqrt{12}) = i^2\sqrt{36} = -1(6) = -6\).
  • Discriminant Interpretation: For \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\): if \(\Delta > 0\), two distinct real roots; if \(\Delta = 0\), one repeated real rational root (الرأس on \(x\)-axis); if \(\Delta < 0\), two non-real complex conjugate roots \(a \pm bi\).
  • Completing the Square with \(a \neq 1\): Always factor the leading المعامل \(a\) out of the quadratic and linear terms before adding \((b/(2a))^2\). In \(2x^2 - 12x\), factor to \(2(x^2 - 6x)\), then add 9 inside the parentheses (which actually adds \(2 \times 9 = 18\) to that side).

label.ar: مثال محلول \(C\) — Quadratics & Complex Numbers (Easy Application)

body.en:
Problem (Easy): Which of the following is equivalent to the expression \((3 + 4i)(2 - 5i)\), where \(i = \sqrt{-1}\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: To multiply two complex numbers, expand using the distributive property (FOIL): \[ (3 + 4i)(2 - 5i) = (3)(2) + (3)(-5i) + (4i)(2) + (4i)(-5i) \] Compute each term: \[ = 6 - 15i + 8i - 20i^2 \] Combine the imaginary parts: \[ -15i + 8i = -7i \] Recall that by definition, \(i^2 = -1\). Substitute \(-1\) for \(i^2\): \[ -20i^2 = -20(-1) = +20 \] Combine the real parts: \[ 6 + 20 = 26 \] Thus, the expression simplifies to: \[ 26 - 7i \] Common Misconceptions: - \(26 + 7i\) results from an arithmetic sign error when combining \(-15i + 8i\). - \(-14 - 7i\) results from incorrectly assuming \(i^2 = 1\), which yields \(6 - 20 = -14\). - \(6 - 20i\) occurs when only multiplying the first terms and the last terms, completely omitting the middle cross-terms.
body.ar:
Problem (Easy): Which of the following is equivalent to the العبارة الجبرية \((3 + 4i)(2 - 5i)\), حيث \(i = \sqrt{-1}\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: To multiply two complex numbers, expand using the distributive property (FOIL): \[ (3 + 4i)(2 - 5i) = (3)(2) + (3)(-5i) + (4i)(2) + (4i)(-5i) \] Compute each term: \[ = 6 - 15i + 8i - 20i^2 \] Combine the imaginary parts: \[ -15i + 8i = -7i \] Recall that by definition, \(i^2 = -1\). عوّض \(-1\) for \(i^2\): \[ -20i^2 = -20(-1) = +20 \] Combine the real parts: \[ 6 + 20 = 26 \] وعليه, the العبارة الجبرية simplifies to: \[ 26 - 7i \] Common Misconceptions: - \(26 + 7i\) results from an arithmetic sign error عندما combining \(-15i + 8i\). - \(-14 - 7i\) results from incorrectly assuming \(i^2 = 1\), which yields \(6 - 20 = -14\). - \(6 - 20i\) occurs عندما only multiplying the first terms and the last terms, completely omitting the middle cross-terms.

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Quadratics & Complex Numbers (Medium Application)
label.ar: مثال محلول \(D\) — Quadratics & Complex Numbers (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): Consider the quadratic equation \[ 2x^2 - (k - 1)x + (k + 1) = 0 \] where \(k\) is a real constant. The equation has two non-real complex conjugate roots. If the imaginary parts of the roots have a magnitude of \(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\), what is the greatest possible value of \(k\)?

Step-by-Step Solution: To find the parameter \(k\), apply the quadratic formula to \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\): \[ x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \] Identify the coefficients from the given equation: \[ a = 2, \quad b = -(k - 1), \quad c = k + 1 \] Compute the discriminant \(\Delta\): \[ \Delta = [-(k - 1)]^2 - 4(2)(k + 1) = (k^2 - 2k + 1) - (8k + 8) = k^2 - 10k - 7 \] Since the equation has non-real complex roots, \(\Delta < 0\), meaning: \[ \sqrt{\Delta} = i\sqrt{-\Delta} = i\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7} \] Substituting this into the quadratic formula gives: \[ x = \frac{k - 1 \pm i\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7}}{2(2)} = \frac{k - 1}{4} \pm \frac{\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7}}{4}i \] The magnitude of the imaginary part is: \[ \frac{\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7}}{4} \] Set this equal to the given value \(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\): \[ \frac{\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7}}{4} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{2} \] Multiply both sides by \(4\): \[ \sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7} = 2\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{28} \] Square both sides: \[ -k^2 + 10k + 7 = 28 \implies k^2 - 10k + 21 = 0 \] Factor the quadratic equation: \[ (k - 3)(k - 7) = 0 \] Thus, \(k = 3\) or \(k = 7\). Both values yield \(-\Delta = 28 > 0\), confirming the roots are non-real. The greatest possible value of \(k\) is \(7\). - Misconception 3 arises from selecting the smaller valid parameter value. - Misconception 10 arises from using \(2\) instead of \(2a = 4\) in the denominator of the quadratic formula, leading to \(-k^2 + 10k + 7 = 7 \implies k = 10\). - Misconception 5 arises from taking the midpoint/axis of symmetry of the two values of \(k\).
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): Consider the المعادلة التربيعية \[ 2x^2 - (k - 1)x + (k + 1) = 0 \] حيث \(k\) is a real الثابت. The المعادلة has two non-real complex conjugate roots. If the imaginary parts of the roots have a magnitude of \(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\), what is the greatest possible value of \(k\)?

Step-by-Step الحل: To أوجد المعامل \(k\), apply the quadratic الصيغة to \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\): \[ x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \] Identify the المعاملات from the المعطيات المعادلة: \[ a = 2, \quad b = -(k - 1), \quad c = k + 1 \] Compute the discriminant \(\Delta\): \[ \Delta = [-(k - 1)]^2 - 4(2)(k + 1) = (k^2 - 2k + 1) - (8k + 8) = k^2 - 10k - 7 \] Since the المعادلة has non-real complex roots, \(\Delta < 0\), meaning: \[ \sqrt{\Delta} = i\sqrt{-\Delta} = i\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7} \] Substituting this into the quadratic الصيغة gives: \[ x = \frac{k - 1 \pm i\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7}}{2(2)} = \frac{k - 1}{4} \pm \frac{\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7}}{4}i \] The magnitude of the imaginary part is: \[ \frac{\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7}}{4} \] Set this equal to the المعطيات value \(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{2}\): \[ \frac{\sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7}}{4} = \frac{\sqrt{7}}{2} \] Multiply both sides by \(4\): \[ \sqrt{-k^2 + 10k + 7} = 2\sqrt{7} = \sqrt{28} \] Square both sides: \[ -k^2 + 10k + 7 = 28 \implies k^2 - 10k + 21 = 0 \] Factor the المعادلة التربيعية: \[ (k - 3)(k - 7) = 0 \] وعليه, \(k = 3\) or \(k = 7\). Both values yield \(-\Delta = 28 > 0\), confirming the roots are non-real. The greatest possible value of \(k\) is \(7\). - Misconception 3 arises from selecting the smaller valid المعامل value. - Misconception 10 arises from using \(2\) instead of \(2a = 4\) in the denominator of the quadratic الصيغة, leading to \(-k^2 + 10k + 7 = 7 \implies k = 10\). - Misconception 5 arises from taking the midpoint/axis of symmetry of the two values of \(k\).

question.en: Solve \(2x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\) by completing the square, expressing all solutions in exact \(a \pm bi\) form.
question.ar: حل \(2x^2 - 6x + 5 = 0\) by compليكنing the square, expressing all solutions in exact \(a \pm bi\) form.

solution.en:
Divide by the leading coefficient 2 or factor it out from the variable terms:

\[2(x^2 - 3x) = -5 \implies x^2 - 3x = -\frac{5}{2}.\]

Add \(\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) to both sides:

\[x^2 - 3x + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{5}{2} + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{10}{4} + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{1}{4}.\]

Write as a perfect square and take the square root of both sides:

\[\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = -\frac{1}{4} \implies x - \frac{3}{2} = \pm\sqrt{-\frac{1}{4}} = \pm\frac{i}{2}.\]\[x = \frac{3}{2} \pm \frac{1}{2}i.\]
solution.ar:
Divide بتطبيق leading coefficient 2 or حلّل it out from the variable terms:

\[2(x^2 - 3x) = -5 \implies x^2 - 3x = -\frac{5}{2}.\]

Add \(\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}\) to both sides:

\[x^2 - 3x + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{5}{2} + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{10}{4} + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{1}{4}.\]

Write as a perfect square and take the square root of both sides:

\[\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = -\frac{1}{4} \implies x - \frac{3}{2} = \pm\sqrt{-\frac{1}{4}} = \pm\frac{i}{2}.\]\[x = \frac{3}{2} \pm \frac{1}{2}i.\]

question.en: [Practice 4 · Easy] What are the solutions to the quadratic equation \(x^2 - 6x + 13 = 0\)?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Quadratics & Complex Numbers): [Practice 4 · Easy] What are the solutions to the quadratic equation \(x^2 - 6x + 13 = 0\)?

hints.en: To solve the quadratic equation \(x^2 - 6x + 13 = 0\), use the quadratic formula \(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\) with \(a = 1\), \(b = -6\), and \(c = 13\): \(x = \dfrac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(1)(13)}}{2(1)} = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 52}}{2} = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{-16}}{2}\).
hints.ar: To حل the quadratic equation \(x^2 - 6x + 13 = 0\), use the quadratic formula \(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\) with \(a = 1\), \(b = -6\), and \(c = 13\): \(x = \dfrac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(1)(13)}}{2(1)} = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 52}}{2} = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{-16}}{2}\).

hints.en: - \(x = 3 \pm 4i\) occurs if the radical term is not divided by the denominator \(2\).
hints.ar: - \(x = 3 \pm 4i\) occurs إذا كان the radical term is not divided بتطبيق denominator \(2\).

solution.en:
To solve the quadratic equation \(x^2 - 6x + 13 = 0\), use the quadratic formula \(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\) with \(a = 1\), \(b = -6\), and \(c = 13\):

\[
x = \dfrac{-(-6) \pm \sqrt{(-6)^2 - 4(1)(13)}}{2(1)} = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{36 - 52}}{2} = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{-16}}{2}
\]

Since \(\sqrt{-16} = 4i\), simplify the expression:

\[
x = \dfrac{6 \pm 4i}{2} = 3 \pm 2i
\]

- \(x = 3 \pm 4i\) occurs if the radical term is not divided by the denominator \(2\).
- \(x = -3 \pm 2i\) occurs from a sign error when computing \(-b\).
- \(x = 3 \pm 2\) occurs from ignoring the imaginary unit \(i\) and treating \(\sqrt{-16}\) as \(4\).

question.en: [Practice 5 · Medium] In the figure, right triangle \(ABC\) has a right angle at vertex \(C\), and altitude \(CD\) is drawn perpendicular to hypotenuse \(AB\). If \(AD = x\), \(DB = x + 5\), and \(CD = 6\), what is the length of hypotenuse \(AB\)?
question.ar: [Practice 5 · Medium] In the figure, right triangle \(ABC\) has a right angle at vertex \(C\), and altitude \(CD\) is drawn عمودي على hypotenuse \(AB\). إذا كان \(AD = x\), \(DB = x + 5\), and \(CD = 6\), what is the length of hypotenuse \(AB\)?

hints.en: By the Geometric Mean Theorem (Altitude Rule) for right triangles, the altitude to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two segments of the hypotenuse: \(CD^2 = AD \cdot DB\).
hints.ar: بتطبيق Geometric Mean Theorem (Altitude Rule) for right triangles, the altitude to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two segments of the hypotenuse: \(CD^2 = AD \cdot DB\).

hints.en: Substitute the given values into the equation: \(6^2 = x(x + 5)\) \(36 = x^2 + 5x\).
hints.ar: عوّض the given values into the equation: \(6^2 = x(x + 5)\) \(36 = x^2 + 5x\).

solution.en:
By the Geometric Mean Theorem (Altitude Rule) for right triangles, the altitude to the hypotenuse is the geometric mean of the two segments of the hypotenuse:
\[ CD^2 = AD \cdot DB \]

Substitute the given values into the equation:
\[ 6^2 = x(x + 5) \]
\[ 36 = x^2 + 5x \]
\[ x^2 + 5x - 36 = 0 \]

Factor the quadratic equation:
\[ (x + 9)(x - 4) = 0 \]

This yields \(x = -9\) or \(x = 4\). Because \(x\) represents a geometric length, it must be positive, so \(x = 4\).

The length of hypotenuse \(AB\) is the sum of segments \(AD\) and \(DB\):
\[ AB = AD + DB = x + (x + 5) = 2x + 5 \]

Substitute \(x = 4\):
\[ AB = 2(4) + 5 = 13 \]

Common Misconceptions:
- Choosing 4 is the trap of solving for \(x\) but failing to find the full hypotenuse length \(AB\).
- Choosing 12 results from confusing the geometric mean with the arithmetic mean, setting \(\frac{AD + DB}{2} = 6\), which gives \(AB = 12\).
- Choosing 23 results from a factoring sign error \((x - 9)(x + 4) = 0\), yielding extraneous root \(x = 9\) and \(AB = 2(9) + 5 = 23\).
solution.ar:

\[ CD^2 = AD \cdot DB \]

عوّض the given values into the equation:

\[ 36 = x^2 + 5x \]

\[ (x + 9)(x - 4) = 0 \]

This yields \(x = -9\) or \(x = 4\). Because \(x\) represents a geometric length, it must be positive, so \(x = 4\).

\[ AB = AD + DB = x + (x + 5) = 2x + 5 \]

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:
تُبنى النماذج الجبرية والمتسامية الأساسية من خلال تطبيق التحويل القياسي \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\) على إحدى الدوال الأم التسع، حيث يتحكم \(|a|\) في التمدد الرأسي (مع انعكاس حول محور السينات إذا كان \(a < 0\))، ويمثل \(h\) الإزاحة الأفقية، و\(k\) الإزاحة الرأسية:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة
الثابتة\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)مستقيم أفقي ميله \(0\)
الخطية\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)ميل ثابت \(m = a\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, k)\)
التربيعية\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)قطع مكافئ رأسه \((h, k)\) ومحوره \(x = h\)
التكعيبية\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)نقطة انعطاف مركزية \((h, k)\)
القيمة المطلقة\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)رأس زاوي على شكل V عند \((h, k)\) بميلين \(\pm a\)
الجذرية\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)نقطة بداية \((h, k)\) ومجال مقيّد \(x \ge h\)
النسبية (المقلوب)\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) وتقارب أفقي \(y = k\)
الأسية\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)تقارب أفقي \(y = k\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, a+k)\)
اللوغاريتمية\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h+1, k)\)
